data.title: Insecure Active Directory Certificate Services Template Configuration
data.summary:
A certificate template permitted standard domain users to request certificates on
behalf of any account, including domain administrators, allowing authentication
as those accounts.
data.description:
Active Directory Certificate Services issues certificates according to templates
that define who may enrol and what the resulting certificate may be used for.
Where a template permits client authentication, allows the requester to supply an
arbitrary subject alternative name, does not require approval by a certificate
manager, and grants enrolment rights to broad groups, the combination allows any
member of those groups to obtain a certificate identifying them as any other
account in the directory.

The resulting certificate is issued by the enterprise certification authority and
is therefore trusted for Kerberos authentication throughout the forest. The holder
can authenticate as the impersonated account without ever knowing its password.

This condition is particularly durable. A certificate remains valid for its full
lifetime regardless of password changes, so an attacker retains access even after
the compromised account's password is reset. Remediation requires revocation of
the certificate in addition to correcting the template.

A template meeting these conditions was identified within the environment and was
enrollable by standard domain users.
data.impact:
Any authenticated domain user could obtain a certificate authenticating them as a
domain administrator, resulting in complete compromise of the Active Directory
forest. Because the certificate remains valid independently of the account's
password, access persists through credential rotation and standard incident
response measures unless the certificate itself is identified and revoked.
data.recommendation:
1. Disable the affected certificate template immediately, or remove client
   authentication from its extended key usage where the template serves another
   legitimate purpose.

2. Remove the "Supply in the request" setting for subject alternative names.
   Certificate subjects should be constructed by the certification authority from
   directory data rather than supplied by the requester.

3. Enable certificate manager approval on any template that permits client
   authentication and is enrollable by non-administrative users.

4. Restrict enrolment rights to purpose-specific security groups, removing broad
   principals such as Domain Users and Authenticated Users.

5. Audit all certificates already issued from the affected template, and revoke
   any that cannot be attributed to a legitimate request. Correcting the template
   alone does not invalidate certificates already obtained.

6. Review all templates in the environment against known misconfiguration classes
   using a tool such as Certify or Certipy, as several distinct escalation paths
   exist beyond the one identified here.
